question: Do the big pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, SmolVLA and pi0.5, match or beat the smaller Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) policy when trained on the tuned SO-101 recipe, and does online reinforcement learning (RL) close SmolVLA's remaining gap?
measure: Offline action-chunk mean squared error (MSE) at chunk start 90 (the first descent toward the cube) on 10 held-out cube poses, closed-loop task successes and pickups out of 30 simulation rollouts (10 held-out poses x 3 repeats, replanning every 30 steps), and horizontal gripper-to-cube error just before jaw closure in millimetres (lateral closure median, against the 8.0 mm grasp tolerance).
outcome: Mixed. On the tuned SO-101 recipe, SmolVLA rose from 2 of 30 (0 of 30 at execute 30) in October to 14 of 30, and 20,000 reinforcement learning episodes pushed it to 19 of 30 (20 pickups, 9.7 mm median closure error). Half-trained pi0.5 (5,000 steps) reached a lower offline loss (7.5e-4 vs 1.6e-3) and tighter closure (6.8 mm) with 16 pickups, but lost 9 pickups at set-down to score 7 of 30; neither beat ACT (21 to 24 of 30).
setup: A policy is the neural network that maps camera images and joint angles to joint commands. Our policies predict an action chunk of 90 future steps at once and run the first 30 steps before replanning from a new image (execute 30). Chunk start 0 is the opening survey move, chunk start 90 is the first descent toward the cube where visual localization matters most, and chunk starts 180, 270 and 360 cover lifting, carrying, setting down and retreating. Offline loss is the mean squared error (MSE) between the policy's chunk and the scripted teacher's chunk; held-out means 10 cube placements the model never trained on. In October (experiments 37 and 40), two pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, pi0.5 (3.38B parameters, 458M trained with Low-Rank Adaptation, or LoRA, rank 16) and SmolVLA (450M parameters, 100M trained with a frozen vision-language backbone), scored 15 of 30 and 2 of 30 (0 of 30 at execute 30) on the older SO-100 scene with unrandomized captures and a 25 mm lift. Since then, the Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) recipe changed in six ways: the SO-101 gripper with a wider 8.0 mm grasp tolerance (experiment 43), a measured servo model (experiments 39 and 44), physics v2 servo-gain randomization from soft to stiff (experiment 45), a 100 mm lift with slow release (experiment 48), execute 30 replanning, and 7,150 randomized placements in capture_v2 (experiment 51). On that recipe, ACT scores 21 to 24 of 30 in simulation. Experiment 56 trains SmolVLA (30,000 steps) and pi0.5 (5,000 steps) on that exact recipe, then runs 20,000 episodes of ReinFlow Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning on SmolVLA's output head (out_head).

parts.title: Do the tuned SO-101 recipe and 30-step replanning fix SmolVLA and pi0.5?
parts.why: In October, SmolVLA scored 2 of 30 (0 of 30 at execute 30) and pi0.5 scored 15 of 30 on the older SO-100 scene. Testing both on the exact capture_v2 dataset and so101_servo_lift100_rel30 scene separates model limitations from task and recipe improvements.
parts.did: Fine-tuned SmolVLA for 30,000 steps (batch 32, 0.96 M samples) and pi0.5 LoRA rank 16 for 5,000 steps (batch 32, 0.16 M samples, cut from October's 10,000 steps to fit the night) on capture_v2 (7,150 placements), then ran 30 rollouts (10 held-out poses x 3 repeats) at execute 30.
parts.conclusion: SmolVLA jumped from 0 of 30 at execute 30 to 14 of 30 with the same model settings, but its closing error stayed at 13.2 mm (13.15 mm), so the gain came from the SO-101 grasp tolerance, slow release and 30-step replanning (which corrected 29.50 mm of lateral RMS error between steps 179 and 250). Half-trained pi0.5 picked up the cube 16 times with half the lateral error (6.8 mm), but lost 9 pickups at set-down. Neither reached ACT.

parts.title: Are the VLAs memorizing the training placements or under-fitting?
parts.why: When closed-loop success lags the baseline, comparing held-out loss against training loss across task stages separates memorization of training scenes (held-out / train ratio far above 1) from under-training or capacity limits (ratio near 1, both high).
parts.did: Scored SmolVLA every 2,500 steps and pi0.5 every 1,000 steps on the 10 held-out poses and the training set at chunk start 0 (survey), start 90 (descent) and starts 180, 270 and 360 (lift, carry, set-down).
parts.conclusion: Error concentrates at chunk start 90 (3.6x to 9.3x higher than start 0 and starts 180 to 360). Because the held-out to train ratio at start 90 is 0.78 for SmolVLA and 0.44 for pi0.5, memorization is ruled out. SmolVLA's frozen backbone settles near a 1.6e-3 floor after 30,000 steps, whereas pi0.5 is still falling fast at 5,000 steps (from 1.1e-3 at 4,000 to 7.5e-4 at 5,000, compared with 2.5e-4 at 10,000 steps in October).

parts.title: Does online reinforcement learning (ReinFlow PPO) fix SmolVLA's failures?
parts.why: SmolVLA's supervised fine-tune had a 13.15 mm median lateral closure error and lost 16 of 30 rollouts (10 safety invalidations, 3 not settled, 3 pickup incomplete). Online RL with physics v2 randomization tests whether trial-and-error can tighten closure and set-down.
parts.did: Ran ReinFlow PPO for 20,000 episodes (334 iterations, 12 parallel environments, 60 episodes per iteration, execute 30) updating SmolVLA's output head (out_head) on 1,600 training poses with bench_physics_v2, scoring a 20-pose monitor suite every 480 episodes and the 30-rollout held-out suite at the end.
parts.conclusion: RL raised SmolVLA from 14 of 30 to 19 of 30 on the held-out suite and from 0.50 to 0.60 on the 20-pose monitor suite (pickup rate 0.50 to 0.65, grasp rate 0.55 to 0.70, invalidation rate 0.40 to 0.30). It cut held-out median lateral closure error from 13.15 mm to 9.69 mm, cut median yaw error from 3.36 deg to 2.11 deg, eliminated all 3 not-settled losses, and cut pickup-incomplete losses from 3 to 1.

parts.title: Why do pi0.5's pickups fail to settle, and why do 10 safety invalidations remain after RL?
parts.why: Aggregate counts hide which poses fail and why. Breaking the 30 rollouts down across the 10 held-out poses shows whether losses come from joint limits, table collisions, vertical height gaps, or set-down placement.
parts.did: Inspected per-pose start-90 loss, closure lateral and vertical errors (lat and dz), and rollout flags (pickup_completed, released, retreated, settled_frames, limiting_frames, unsafe_contact_frames) in evaluation.json for all three runs.
parts.conclusion: In all 9 of pi0.5's not-settled episodes (pose_001, pose_003, pose_009), the arm lifted the cube 82.4 to 84.1 mm, entered the placement region, released and retreated, leaving the cube stationary on the table but outside the target square center (settled_frames: 0 at 480 actions). On pose_007 and pose_008, pi0.5 aimed within 2.14 to 3.77 mm laterally but had a 10.39 to 12.41 mm vertical gap (dz) and hit 30 to 32 unsafe contact frames. Output-head RL fixed SmolVLA on pose_004 (0/3 to 3/3), pose_007 (2/3 to 3/3) and pose_005 (0/3 to 1/3), but could not reroute the gross joint-limit and contact failures on pose_000, pose_003 and pose_009.

trust.text: Same 7,150-placement capture_v2 training manifest, so101_servo_lift100_rel30 scene (hash de39e898) and 10 held-out poses x 3 repeats at execute 30 as the tuned ACT baseline
Both fine-tunes logged in-training held-out and train loss curves across chunk boundaries (start 0, start 90, starts 180/270/360) plus closed-loop closure kinematics in millimetres
RL on SmolVLA completed all 20,000 episodes (334 iterations) under bench_physics_v2 randomization and was scored on both the 20-pose monitor suite and the 30-rollout held-out suite
Sample budgets were not equal: ACT saw 5.1 M samples, SmolVLA saw 0.96 M samples (plus 20,000 RL episodes), and pi0.5 saw only 0.16 M samples (5,000 steps, half of October's 10,000 steps)
One training seed (seed 202), 10 held-out poses, and simulation only (no real-arm rollouts or real-frame gate in this run)
Per-rollout telemetry/*.json files and original task-spooler lines for job IDs 256 to 264 were not in the input bundle, and pi05_ft/progress.json kept step 4000 beside the step-5000 final block

meaning: The recipe changes that made ACT work (wider SO-101 gripper tolerance, physics v2 servo randomization, 100 mm lift with slow release, and replanning every 30 steps) also make SmolVLA work (0 of 30 to 14 of 30), and 20,000 episodes of ReinFlow PPO on the output head bring SmolVLA to 19 of 30 by tightening closure error from 13.15 mm to 9.69 mm and eliminating set-down failures. However, ACT remains better (21 to 24 of 30, 5.2 mm closure median) and safer. Do not switch from ACT to SmolVLA while 10 of 30 held-out rollouts still end in safety invalidation, and finish training pi0.5 to 10,000 steps before running RL on it.
lesson: When a model jumps from 0 of 30 to 14 of 30 after a recipe change while its 13.2 mm grasp error stays unchanged, the environment tolerance and replanning loop did the work, not better perception; always measure jaw-to-object error directly in task units.

next.title: Resume pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning from 5,000 to 10,000 steps
next.why: At 5,000 steps (0.16 M samples), pi0.5 already has half of SmolVLA's start-90 loss (7.5e-4 vs 1.6e-3) and 6.8 mm lateral closure error, and its loss is still dropping fast toward October's 2.5e-4.

next.title: Inspect per-frame telemetry on pi0.5's 9 not-settled episodes (pose_001, pose_003, pose_009)
next.why: All 9 completed pickup and released the cube stationary on the table, but missed the settled-in-square tolerance around square_center_xy.

next.title: Unfreeze more than out_head or add safety-margin shaping for VLA RL
next.why: Output-head PPO fixed near-misses (14 of 30 to 19 of 30) but left all 10 held-out safety invalidations (pose_000 joint limits and pose_003/pose_009 table contacts) unchanged.
